Darkfost: Binance Bitcoin Open Interest Drops Nearly 40%, Marking the Largest Dollar-Denominated Deleveraging in Bitcoin's History

CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost said Binance's Bitcoin open interest has fallen by nearly $4.5 billion over the past year and remains down nearly 40%. In July, the decline exceeded 45%, equivalent to $6.25 billion, marking the largest deleveraging event in Bitcoin's history in dollar terms. Binance accounts for over 34% of total Bitcoin open interest. Darkfost attributed the contraction to macroeconomic uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, tighter monetary policy, voluntary position closures, forced liquidations, and declining Bitcoin prices. In 2026 alone, the broader crypto market has recorded at least eight days with liquidations exceeding $1.5 billion. — link

Darkfost: Binance Bitcoin Open Interest Drops Nearly 40%, Marking the Largest Dollar-Denominated Deleveraging in Bitcoin's History

CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost said Binance's Bitcoin open interest has fallen by nearly $4.5 billion over the past year and remains down nearly 40%. In July, the decline exceeded 45%, equivalent to $6.25 billion, marking the largest deleveraging event in Bitcoin's history in dollar terms. Binance accounts for over 34% of total Bitcoin open interest. Darkfost attributed the contraction to macroeconomic uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, tighter monetary policy, voluntary position closures, forced liquidations, and declining Bitcoin prices. In 2026 alone, the broader crypto market has recorded at least eight days with liquidations exceeding $1.5 billion. — link

Bloomberg: Trump Memecoin Dinner Returns as Demand Falls and Political Scrutiny Rises

Donald Trump is set to attend another dinner for top TRUMP memecoin holders as participation declines sharply and the token trades about 99% below its 2025 peak. Crypto trader Morten Christensen told Bloomberg that hedging his TRUMP holdings reduced his net cost of qualifying from about $1,200 for the first dinner and $500 for the second to a roughly $6 profit this time.

Democratic lawmakers have renewed conflict-of-interest concerns over token holders receiving private access to the president, while the White House said the privately organized event is not a government function. — link
